_comment: Everything spoken in the first fifteen minutes. Text lives here and never in a script, so a rewrite of Grandpa's voice is a data edit and a translator never has to read GDScript.
_comment_shape: A conversation is a speaker, a portrait, and an ordered list of lines. NO branching: docs/OPENING_SEQUENCE.md is explicit that the only choice in this sequence is which creature, and that one is made through scripts/ui/starter_picker.gd's orb preview, not a dialogue branch (SA0-orbs, 2026-08-11; before that it was made by walking up to a body in the meadow, which is what this comment used to describe). The previous prototype's DialogueRunner supported choices and this port deliberately drops them — the moment a line can branch, the starter choice starts wanting to be a text menu instead of something you look at first.
_comment_lines: A line is a string, or an object when it needs to override the speaker/portrait or emit an effect. Effects are opaque strings handed back to whoever started the conversation; this file knows that finishing the briefing emits `beat:starter_choice` and that the first-catch line emits `give:orb_basic:15`, and the dialogue system has no idea what a beat or an item is. A `give:` effect sits on the exact line that speaks the gift, so the satchel fills as he says it rather than in a lump after the box closes.
_comment_voice: He is warm and brief. The opening gives exactly one clear objective at a time: choose a starter, catch a second creature, see Mira, then sign up for the tournament.

grandpa_house._comment: Required first conversation. It establishes the immediate threat and moves directly into starter selection; later conversations teach the next action one at a time.
grandpa_house.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: They've taken Meadows Hall, and the land's already starting to suffer.
I'd go after them myself if I were twenty years younger.
If you're going to take this on, you won't do it alone.

lines.text: Come on. It's time you chose your first creature.

grandpa_waiting._comment: Talking to him again before choosing. Short on purpose: a player who came back to hear the briefing twice is a player the game is wasting. Practically unreachable since SA0-orbs -- the picker opens the instant this conversation closes and is modal, so there is no real window left to talk to him again mid-choice. Kept rather than deleted: harmless, and cheap insurance if the picker's timing ever changes.
grandpa_waiting.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Still deciding? Take your time — have another look at all three.

grandpa_first_catch._comment: The required return after naming. The fifteen Basic Orbs arrive here, just before their first use, rather than being buried in the starter exposition.
grandpa_first_catch.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Before you go anywhere, you need another creature beside you.

lines.text: Take these Orbs. Head outside, find one you like, and catch it.
Then come back and show me.

grandpa_encounter_hint._comment: Talking to him between the naming and the catch. He does not repeat the whole briefing.
grandpa_encounter_hint.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Down the path, past the rise. Get close and it'll stop and look at you — that's your moment.

grandpa_after_first_catch._comment: The required return after the first catch. Mira owns the tool/recipe reward; this only points the player to her.
grandpa_after_first_catch.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Nice catch. That's how a team starts.
Now go see Mira in the village. She'll give you some basic tools and teach you how to make more Orbs.

grandpa_tournament._comment: The required return after Mira. The registrar owns the qualification explanation and the broadened checklist.
grandpa_tournament.speaker: Grandpa Elias
lines: Good. Now you can take care of yourself out there.
If you really want to go after Team Tether, start by proving you can handle a team.
Go sign up for the village tournament.

lines.text: They'll tell you what you need to enter.
